projects.name: Apex FSD - StormHacks 2026 (Winner)
projects.description: A self-driving AI that plays Forza Horizon by physically turning a real steering wheel, and hands control back the instant a human grabs it. A PyTorch model learns to steer from screen pixels and live game telemetry, and every manual correction is fed back in as new training data. When the car kept drifting toward roadside signs, saliency maps showed what the model was looking at so we could remove the footage that taught it. Won Best Python Hack at StormHacks.

projects.name: Scheming - HackMIT 2026
projects.description: A lie detector for AI models that flags when what a model says contradicts its own private reasoning, and points to the exact line as evidence. We tested it on AI agents playing Werewolf, where bluffing is part of the game, then ran it on real coding-agent sessions to catch agents claiming work was done when their own logs said otherwise.

projects.name: YouTube Shorts AI Optimizer
projects.description: An AI agent that reviews draft YouTube Shorts before they go live, predicts where viewers will swipe away, and suggests fixes. I built it for my own channel and later opened it up to other creators. It runs as a remote MCP server on Google Cloud Run, with traced agent steps, retry-safe background workers, and guardrails that keep untrusted comment text from hijacking the agent.

projects.name: GitIntent - UC Berkeley AI LLM Hackathon 2026
projects.description: A shared memory layer for AI coding agents that records every code change together with the prompt and reasoning behind it. Before an agent attempts a task, it can look up similar past work, including failed attempts, so it doesn't repeat the same mistakes. Retrieval combines vector and keyword search on Redis Stack.

projects.name: Inventory & Sales Automation Platform
projects.description: Custom infrastructure for my resale business on Grailed, Depop, and eBay. A Go worker reads sale emails from Gmail and turns them into orders automatically, a Playwright service reposts listings on a schedule and steps prices down over time, and a Spring Boot and React dashboard shows inventory, orders, and profit, with Redis caching keeping the reports fast.

projects.name: Premier Predictor
projects.description: Scrapes and cleans English Premier League match data, then trains a Random Forest model with pandas and scikit-learn to predict match outcomes.

projects.name: Java OOP Quiz Application
projects.description: A Java study tool for CPSC 210 students that quizzes them on object-oriented programming concepts. Built with a layered architecture, interface-based abstraction, JSON save/load, and a full JUnit test suite.

projects.name: Vital-Sense Radar
projects.description: A non-contact monitor that estimates breathing and heart rate from Wi-Fi signals. A pair of ESP32-S3 boards send and receive the signal, and Python processes the Channel State Information into vitals. No camera or wearable needed.

projects.name: Chelsea FC Play Predictor
projects.description: A data pipeline that pulls Chelsea match data from FBref and Understat into PostgreSQL and computes features automatically, feeding a set of statistical and ML models that predict match events. An expected-value optimizer and a Streamlit dashboard sit on top.

projects.name: Photo Time Capsule
projects.description: A hackathon mobile app for making time-capsule photo albums. Users capture photos with the camera and discuss them in comment threads. Built with React Native, Firebase, and Expo Go.

projects.name: Minecraft Data Science Project
projects.description: Analyzed player engagement and subscription behavior on a Minecraft research server, using KNN classification with cross-validation to predict which players would subscribe. Built in R with tidymodels.
